thread: Follow a bird from its nest into the air and across a migration route. The swarm meets patterned eggs and ingenious nests, takes on feathers and beaks, and travels between distant habitats with the birds.

candidates.name: Australian Museum
candidates.why: Its ornithology collection includes eggs, feathers and nests, including a nest built in an old boot and magpie nests made of wire; its animal profiles offer many birds to hatch into.

candidates.name: American Bird Conservancy
candidates.why: A bird library ranges across the Americas and Hawai‘i, with distinctive beaks, plumage and behaviors, while habitat pages offer forests, grasslands and wetlands to inhabit.

candidates.name: British Trust for Ornithology
candidates.why: Bird ringing, tracking and migration projects follow birds on their travels, with species information and field methods that could become tags, routes and winged travelers.

candidates.name: Birds Canada
candidates.why: Bird monitoring programs, important bird places and conservation technology offer migratory species, observation stations and habitats across Canada.

candidates.name: All About Birds
candidates.why: Cornell's bird identification articles and natural-history features introduce birds through their shapes, calls, feeding strategies and lives in the wild.

candidates.name: Bird Conservancy of the Rockies
candidates.why: Bird banding, monitoring and grassland projects bring together songbirds, field equipment and the landscapes birds cross.

candidates.name: National Audubon Society
candidates.why: Its North American bird guide and habitat material describe a wide variety of birds, their feeding, nesting and migration.

candidates.name: BirdLife International
candidates.why: Birds and conservation projects from many regions offer the swarm islands, flyways and species from across the world.
